item.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption reviews discretion and corruption safeguards in state-level planning approvals, following work with the Department of Planning.
item.support: This report has been prepared in its entirety by the Commission.

item.text: It examines project declarations, assessment and decisions under Part 3A, together with processes for listing state-significant sites.
item.support: Examine the Part 3A process from project declaration to determination
item.section: Terms of reference of joint task force

item.text: The Commission identifies broad discretion, complex rules and outdated local plans as risks, while stating that corrupt use of the powers had not been established.
item.support: There are no established examples of the corrupt use or manipulation of discretion under Part 3A or the MD SEPP

item.text: Its 20 recommendations address planning controls, independent scrutiny, transparency, the Planning and Assessment Commission and third-party appeal rights for private projects.
item.support: the recommendations contained in this report are only directed towards private sector projects.

item.quote: The greater the departure from the previous norm, the greater the corruption risk.
